text: The composite includes objectively recorded death and a protocol-defined BPD component at 36 weeks PMA

BPD criteria incorporate oxygen/respiratory-support thresholds after at least 28 days of support; where oxygen need is subjective, an oxygen-reduction test confirms dependency using an oxygen-saturation threshold

This is a structured, clinically relevant method for the outcome, though the BPD component requires some clinical judgment and the protocol does not establish external validation for this exact trial implementation
The evidence therefore supports probably not inappropriate.
The oxygen-reduction test flowchart was not visually inspectable in the tool response; the applicable textual criteria were inspected.
The same 36-week assessment point, BPD criteria, and oxygen-reduction approach apply to both randomized groups; trial personnel and outcome assessors were blinded
For eligible infants, oxygen-reduction testing was not performed in similar proportions (13/86 vs 13/94)
No group-specific threshold or assessment method is reported
This supports probably no differential measurement; the exact assessment opportunity for every participant is not fully detailed.

Outcome information was unavailable for some participants and reasons for all missing oxygen assessments are not fully reported; this relates chiefly to D3 availability rather than showing differential measurement.
The report states that the persons assessing outcomes were unaware of randomization assignments
This addresses assessor awareness directly; it does not rely solely on the endpoint being objective.
The protocol states that an SAP would be developed before the first participant was randomized and that final amendments would be completed before unblinding

The applicable SAP (edition 3.0, dated 23 July 2019) prespecifies this time-to-first primary composite and its Cox-model hazard ratio analysis, and the report says the trial was conducted and reported according to the protocol and SAP
The article's reported primary analysis follows the planned ITT, adjudicated-endpoint approach and reports the planned HR/CI
This supports prespecification before unblinding; exact investigator access timing is not separately documented.

The exact date of finalization of SAP edition 3.0 relative to unblinded outcome data access is not directly stated in the SAP header, although the protocol commits to final amendments before unblinding.
The protocol and SAP define the primary measurement as the time to first event in the composite of cardiovascular death, HF hospitalization, or urgent HF visit
They distinguish component analyses and a separate secondary composite; the report identifies and reports the prespecified primary composite and its components
There is no evidence that a different eligible primary definition or time point was selected based on results.

The SAP specifies the primary time-to-first-event analysis using an ITT full analysis set and a Cox model stratified by diabetes status and adjusted for prior HF hospitalization, with HR and 95% CI reported
The article reports that the trial followed its SAP and describes the same ITT Cox approach
Other component, secondary, recurrent-event, and subgroup analyses are separately identified; there is no evidence the primary numerical result was chosen from eligible alternatives based on results.
